issue.title: Search the literature for the rewritten forms of arXiv:2611.07007's Eq. (16)
issue.body:
**What.** A literature search for the rewritten forms of arXiv:2611.07007v1's Eq. (16), the geometric echo profile β̃ = A* Re[e^{iθ}/(1 + w e^{2iθ})] with w = q e^{iδ} (notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §2). The question is whether any of them appears elsewhere, as the same function or as the same idea applied to an echo or a periodic profile:
- **A.** The inverse of an ellipse, 1/(e^{−iθ} + w e^{iθ}).
- **B.** The real form (cos θ + q cos(θ + δ))/(1 + q² + 2q cos(2θ + δ)).
- **C.** The odd-harmonic Fourier series with one complex ratio −w.
- **D.** The linear equation (d²/dθ² + 1)[(1 + q² + 2q cos(2θ + δ)) β̃] = 0.
- **E.** The arctan closed form of its integral.

Search at least these areas:
- **Critical collapse and discrete self-similarity:** Choptuik, Gundlach, Hirschmann and Eardley, Martín-García and Gundlach, Reiterer and Trubowitz, and large-D critical collapse.
- **Large-D gravity:** Emparan, Suzuki and Tanabe, and its effective-theory profiles.
- **Echo or self-similar profiles fitted by a geometric harmonic series** in other fields, such as nonlinear waves, breathers and period-doubling.
- **The standard identities behind the forms:** the Poisson kernel, the conjugate Poisson kernel, and the generating functions of geometric Fourier series. These are likely textbook as identities. Record where, and say whether anyone has applied them to an echo profile.

**Why.** AGENTS.md's novelty rule. No sentence saying a form is new, "not found in print" or "first" may go anywhere until the closest prior work has been read and recorded. The published write-up on Eq. (16) only says A, D and E are not in the paper itself (confirmed by #165). This task finds out whether that holds beyond the paper.

**Acceptance (each can fail).**
- The searches are listed (databases, queries, dates), so a second search can repeat them.
- Every candidate is read, not recalled. It is recorded in notes/LIT_REVIEW.md as a new addendum, kept in that file's search and read ledgers (§5, §6), with what it does and does not contain, and its reference is verified against the publisher, arXiv or INSPIRE (notes/REF_CHECK.md). Anything unverified is marked *(unverified)*.
- A verdict per form: found (with the source and its equation), found as a general identity only, or not found in the sources searched. "Not found" is never written as "new".
- No novelty sentence is added to the README, the papers or the notes by this task.

**Depends on.** #165.

comments.body: started. Subagent of the coordinator, on the Apple M5 Mac (`mac`). Checkout: worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-a9e8776c6cd203fb4` of the main repository, branch backed up to `wip/i172`. Threads: 1 (a reading task, no computation). Raw notes go to `I172-mac/` of choptuik-large-d-raw.

Progress (mac, 20:29 UTC; cpu: one reading thread, no computation; memory: negligible).

Round 1 done: 30 searches and about 30 reads across critical collapse (Gundlach 1997, Martín-García–Gundlach 2003, Reiterer–Trubowitz, Price–Pullin, EEGJ, the 2025 review), large D (EEG 2601.14358, Lai–Wen, Wu, Rozali–Way, Emparan–Suzuki–Tanabe), echoes in other fields (gravitational-wave echo templates, Fabry–Pérot round-trip sums, feedback comb filters, breathers) and the identities (DLMF 1.15.12, 18.12.7–10, 4.24.3).

Leads so far, not yet verdicts: Martín-García–Gundlach 2003 Eq. (59) models the high harmonics of the Choptuik spacetime by the Poisson-kernel sum; the Fabry–Pérot transmitted field is a sum over round trips of the same complex form as Eq. (16); Rozali–Way's oscillaton is the δ = 0 case of the arctan form. Raw logs: `I172-mac/` of choptuik-large-d-raw (c7fb914). Next: the remaining identity sources, a second round of synonym queries, then the addendum to notes/LIT_REVIEW.md.

## Closing summary (mac, subagent of the coordinator)

The verdicts are below. Two outside instances matter most. Martín-García and Gundlach (2003) applied the geometric-harmonic idea to the D = 4 echo, and the Fabry–Pérot transmitted field is the same complex function as Eq. (16). No form is called new anywhere. The strongest statement made is "not found in the sources searched".

The record is the new addendum at the end of `notes/LIT_REVIEW.md`, plus a #172 entry in its search ledger (§5) and its read ledger (§6). It is on `wip/i172`, head `e9ea210`. Raw logs, the quotes and an identity check are in choptuik-large-d-raw, `I172-mac/`, commit `4e33763`.

### Verdict per form

| Form | Verdict | Where |
|---|---|---|
| A, the reciprocal of an ellipse | **Found as the same complex function in optics.** The ellipse reading is found as a general identity only. | The Fabry–Pérot transmitted field −t1t2 e^(−iφ)/(1 − r1r2 e^(−2iφ)), a sum over round trips, with θ = −φ and w = −r1r2 (Wikipedia, citing Svelto *(unverified)*; Fratini et al., PRL 113, 243601 (2014), supplement Eq. (S.2)). The inverse of a centred ellipse is Booth's elliptic lemniscate (Coffman). Not found applied to an echo or a self-similar profile. |
| B, the real form | **Found in EEG26b (S58).** Elsewhere it is found only at δ = 0 and π, implicitly, and as a general identity. | At δ = 0 it is the time derivative of Rozali–Way's oscillaton, their Eq. (10). At δ = π it is the derivative of the sine-Gordon breather at its centre. Both are *inferred*: the sources write the field, not its derivative. The denominator is the Poisson kernel's (DLMF 1.15.12). Not found with a general δ. |
| C, odd harmonics with ratio −w | **Found in EEG26b (S58). Its parts are older.** | Gundlach 1997, Sec. II.3: only odd frequencies in the scalar field. **Martín-García–Gundlach 2003, Sec. IV.2**: at D = 4 the coefficients decay exponentially, with phases linear in k, and are compared with the Poisson-kernel sum Σ e^(−a\|k\|) e^(4πikτ/Δ) = sinh a/(cosh a − cos(4πτ/Δ)), Eq. (59). The same series appears as the Fabry–Pérot round-trip sum. Not found as a profile with one complex ratio from the first harmonic on. |
| D, the linear equation | **Not found in the sources searched. Found as a general method only.** | Behind it are Fourier–Padé quotients of trigonometric polynomials (Geer, ICASE 93-68, 1993) and the ODE-to-recurrence method for "trigonometric holonomic" functions (Koepf–Nana Chiadjeu 2015, *(unverified)*, not read). |
| E, the arctan integral | **Found as a general identity, and at δ = 0 and π.** Not found for general δ. | The identity is DLMF 4.24.3 applied termwise. At δ = 0 it is Rozali–Way's oscillaton, artanh(c sin), at fixed r (already in EEG_PROFILE.md §2 (INT)). At δ = π it is the sine-Gordon breather at x = 0, 4 arctan(k sin at), with k = 2√q/(1−q) (*inferred*). It is not in EEG26b (#165). |

The four inferred identities are the oscillaton and breather derivatives, the Fabry–Pérot map, and B written with the Poisson and conjugate kernels. `I172-mac/identity_check.py` checks them at 30 digits and exits 0. Its control flips the sign of q or w, and all four checks then fail (exit 1).

### Closest works

- **EEG26b** (arXiv:2611.07007v1, P5, the source).
  - Contains: Eq. (16), and in (S58) the series and the real form.
  - Does not contain: the reciprocal, the ODE, the antiderivative, the Poisson kernel, or any citation for the geometric model. This agrees with #165.
- **Martín-García & Gundlach**, PRD 68, 024011 (2003) (P3 for B and C).
  - Contains: exponential decay of the τ-harmonics, with decay exponents 0.28–2.04 and phases linear in k, and their comparison with Eq. (59), the Poisson-kernel sum.
  - Does not contain: a fit. The model has a real ratio, sums all k, and has no first-harmonic numerator and no phase δ. They write "We have not found an explanation for this behavior".
- **Rozali & Way**, JHEP 11 (2018) 106 (P3 for E at δ = 0).
  - Contains: φ₀ = artanh(ε e^(−ω²r²/2) sin(ωτ − τ₀)), and δ₀ with the same denominator.
  - Does not contain: the derivative, a harmonic expansion ("a single frequency"), or δ ≠ 0.
- **Fabry–Pérot** (Wikipedia, citing Svelto; Fratini et al. 2014) (P3 for A and C).
  - Contains: the same complex function and the round-trip series.
  - Does not contain: a time profile (φ is an optical phase), the real part as the observable, the ODE or the arctan.
- **Sine-Gordon breather** (Lu–Cuevas-Maraver–Kevrekidis, J. Phys. A 47, 455101 (2014), Eq. (2)) (P2).
  - Contains: E at δ = π.
  - Does not contain: a closed-form harmonic series.
- **Gravitational-wave echo templates** (Mark et al., PRD 96, 084002 (2017), Eqs. (20), (29); Testa–Pani, PRD 98, 044018 (2018)) (P2).
  - Contains: the echo transfer function summed as a geometric series over echoes.
  - Does not contain: periodicity in ω, odd harmonics only, or a real part.
- **Feedback comb filter** (Smith, *Physical Audio Signal Processing*, CCRMA) (P2).
  - Contains: "a series of echoes, exponentially decaying and uniformly spaced in time".
  - Does not contain: Eq. (16)'s function, which would be the delayed variant z^(−1)/(1 + w z^(−2)) (*inferred*).
- **Negative reads**:
  - Price–Pullin (one sinusoid);
  - EEG's PRL and Lai–Wen (the two-mode model);
  - Wu 2610.20705 (any smooth periodic β);
  - Emparan–Suzuki–Tanabe (Gaussian blobs);
  - EEGJ, the 2025 review and Fodor's oscillon review, in the parts read.

### Search ledger

| Channel | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| WebSearch queries | 35 | 1 in extended mode. Areas: critical collapse 4, large D 3, echoes elsewhere 6, breathers/period doubling/log-periodicity 9, identities 9, the forms verbatim 4. |
| INSPIRE REST API through WebFetch | 7 | Forward chains of 2611.07007 (0 citations), EEG's PRL (5), Martín-García–Gundlach 2003 (49 titles) and Rozali–Way (13). |
| Sources opened | 32 | Some in part, some as abstracts. |
| Failed fetches | about 15 | Binary PDFs, Optica placeholders, bot checks, a MacTutor 404, a Springer login. |

All queries were run on 2026-11-08 and are listed verbatim in LIT_REVIEW.md §5. Two rounds were run, and round 2 still added instances, so the search is not dry.

A correction to my 20:29 progress post: it said "30 searches and about 30 reads". At that time the counts were about 22 and 25.

INSPIRE works through WebFetch with `refersto:recid:<n>`. The form `refersto:arxiv:<id>` is ignored, and the API then returns an unfiltered list. LIT_REVIEW.md §8 (2026-10-21) records INSPIRE as blocked, so that gap can now be closed.

### Discrepancies (reported, not fixed)

1. notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §5 marks Price–Pullin's content *(unverified)*. It has now been read in full: one frequency, and no profile of the Eq. (16) type. Proposed text is in the addendum.
2. EEG26b give no source for their geometric law. Martín-García–Gundlach 2003, Sec. IV.2, had observed exponential decay with linear phases at D = 4 and compared it with the Poisson-kernel sum. The repository's own leading-structure passages do not credit that observation. Those are README "Leading structure and a prediction" and the math paper's "The shape of the echo". Proposed credit text is in the addendum, for the coordinator to decide.
3. No discrepancy with #165 or with notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §2: the paper contains B and C only.

`check_numbers.py --selftest` passes 1043 of 1043. `wrap_prose.py` reports no LIT_REVIEW lines over 120.

### Recommended tasks

1. **Read the PDF-only sources of #172.**
   - What: on a machine with a PDF text extractor, read these and record them in LIT_REVIEW.md §6:
     - the Akhmediev-breather spectra (Dudley et al., Opt. Express 17, 21497 (2009); Akhmediev et al. 2011, "universal triangular spectra");
     - Feigenbaum's period-doubling spectrum (1979–1980);
     - Gradshteyn–Ryzhik 1.447–1.448;
     - a textbook derivation of the Fabry–Pérot amplitude (Born–Wolf or Svelto).
   - Why: these are the likeliest further instances of a geometric harmonic law from a rational periodic profile, and they were unreadable here.
   - Acceptance: each source is either quoted with its equation and classified against forms A–E, or marked FULL-TEXT-UNREAD with the failure. The check fails if the Akhmediev sideband law is not quoted with its equation number.
   - Depends on: #172.
2. **Fifth LIT_REVIEW round with INSPIRE cited-by.**
   - What: run `refersto:recid:` for Rozali–Way, EEG's PRL, EEGJ and Clark–Pimentel (the round owed in §8), plus Gundlach 1997 and Reiterer–Trubowitz. Log every citing title and read each P3-or-closer candidate.
   - Why: §8 records INSPIRE as blocked, and it now works.
   - Acceptance: each logged list has the length of the record's INSPIRE `citation_count`, and every candidate graded P3 or above has a read entry. The check fails on a count mismatch or an unread candidate.
   - Depends on: #172.
3. **Finish the partial reads of Martín-García–Gundlach 2003 and Hirschmann–Eardley.**
   - What: read MGG 2003 past character 100000 (the rest of Sec. IV and Figs. 7–9), to see whether the decay rates are tied to complex τ singularities or fitted. Read the body of Hirschmann–Eardley (the arXiv PDF).
   - Why: MGG 2003 is the closest work in critical collapse, and only part of it was read.
   - Acceptance: a quote on whether Eq. (59) is fitted or tied to singularities is added to the addendum. The check fails if the remaining text is not reached.
   - Depends on: #172.

Removing `running` and leaving the issue open for review.

Coordinator review. I reran `I172-mac/identity_check.py` (exit 0) and its control (exit 1). Merged as 6a237d7. Discrepancy 2 is acted on: the README's "Leading structure and a prediction" and the math paper's "The shape of the echo" now credit Martín-García and Gundlach 2003, Sec. IV.2 and Eq. (59). Discrepancy 1, Price–Pullin, is recorded in the addendum. The recommended tasks are #193 (tasks 1 and 3) and #194 (task 2).
